title: Drummers with Oliver, Morton and Hilaire; Jeffery Tavern band
summary: They discuss the drummer's employers and Hilaire, who played in Chicago with Jimmy Noone.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: H&T Tavern, huh? Yeah, that's right. Who did he work with that you know of?

King Oliver, General Morton, and a fella you don't know of. Huey Swift. He was the first Negro band in Chicago that went on the air. First one. He had a beat playing. I was good at him. Jeffery Tavern, the name was Jeffery Tavern, South Chicago and Jeffery. And the car dope, and the place closed it down.
Did you see him with Jelly Roll Morton or did he tell you about it? Oh Cliff?
Yeah. I saw him playing with him. Were you in the band?
But John Jelly Roll after Cliff. Cliff wasn't there when I joined him. But yeah, I saw him playing with Jelly Roll.

Did you know Hilaire Andrew? Sure, I knew Hilaire. He was a nice drummer. Where was he from? Here. And who did he play with in Lionhead? Did you know him back then? Well, Hilaire, I believe he played some too with this Jelly Roll.
And he played most with this man, played Clannett, what's his name, Dyer, when he was going to California? Jimmy Noon.
He played most with Jimmy Noon. Hilaire. Yeah. Yeah, the man played a nice band there, but he didn't get off either.
He just played a nice horn, that's all. That's funny about Hilaire because you never hear about him down here, but he worked with all the New Orleans guys up there. Yeah. Played with them up there.

Well, how he got with me, I don't know. He might have left four hours from here. I don't know. I didn't know anybody from here, but I knew he was from New Orleans. When I was from Chicago, everybody said, you know what? Another one I didn't know, Soncio, Johnny Soncio. I didn't know him.
